text:
It's playing out just as advertised: clear and 70 at this hour, well past what early November usually gives us, and the high near 72 is in record territory for the date. The sun does most of the work, so a lunchtime walk is easy in a light layer. Later this afternoon the temperature may ease back toward the mid 60s, and the sun sets a little after 4:30, so use the daylight.

Clouds fill in tonight and it stays mild, with a low around 57 and a breezy south wind that keeps things from cooling off.

Thursday is the change. The morning starts dry, then showers move in around 8, with the best odds from about 9 to noon. Most of us pick up a tenth to maybe a third of an inch, so it's a nuisance more than a washout. The Euro is wetter than the others, but the rain looks close to certain either way. Expect a high near 66, then another round of scattered showers and patchy fog or drizzle into the evening.

Friday looks mostly dry and still mild, and the weekend turns cooler with showers Saturday. Keep the umbrella by the door for Thursday morning.

week.blurb: Mostly sunny and unseasonably warm with a high near 72, easing to the mid 60s this afternoon before clouds thicken tonight.
Showers arrive after 7am and linger into the night, but amounts stay under a tenth of an inch, with a high near 66.
Patchy morning fog, then mostly cloudy and mild with a high near 64; the daytime looks mostly dry, with showers possible after 7pm.
Cloudy and a good deal cooler, with a high near 53 and about a fifty-fifty shot at rain, so keep a jacket handy.
Looks like any leftover rain wraps up around lunchtime, then mostly cloudy and chilly with a high near 51.
Trending partly sunny and cooler, high near 49, with only a small chance of a stray shower.
If the pattern holds, partly sunny with a high near 51, a shower possible after 7am, and a frosty low around 32 by night.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-04T11:22:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Near record high temperatures are expected today with mostly sunny conditions and limited, localized fire weather concerns.
  2. Showers are expected on Thursday and possibly linger into Thursday night, then mainly dry weather will follow for Friday. No impactful weather is expected.
  3. Periodic showers are possible over the weekend into early next week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 223 AM EST Wednesday... Today's high temperatures were slightly increased.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Record high temperatures for the date remain on track for today; see Climate section of the forecast discussion for details. Progged 925 millibar temperatures of 16 to 18 Celsius, near climatological maximum values, supports high temperatures in the low to mid 70s with dry adiabatic lapse rates across our valley locations. The most unusually extreme temperatures are favored for the Adirondacks and northeastern Vermont, where the Extreme Forecast Index most recent run shows a high confidence of near record high temperatures. This has trended more extreme with time, so we have used the 90th percentile temperature guidance for high temperatures. The resulting forecast highs look consistent with recent verification of observed temperatures and for a scenario with sunshine and warm air advection from the southwest. Relative humidity will remain fairly moderate based on guidance and observed values upstream in the Midwest, putting a likely minimum in the 40% range. A few wind gusts may exceed 25 MPH this morning with channeled flow in the Champlain Valley, but winds aloft generally look too light to cause much concern even if boundary layer mixing is deeper than modeled. KEY MESSAGE 2: A weakening cold front will put an end to our dry and very warm weather. Two rounds of showers appears on the docket for Thursday, with the first round being relatively disordered showers tied to a surge of anomalous moisture sliding northeastward through our region. This precipitation looks strongly forced with relatively deep moisture such that rain chances will be nearly certain for at least a brief period of time during the daytime hours. Towards evening, while moisture will be more limited, sufficiently steep lapse rates to yield a ribbon of instability and a chance of loosely organized showers that will track to the east across northern Vermont Thursday night. As the front exits/washes out to our east, think flow will be light enough amidst rich near surface moisture to support some patchy fog and drizzle regardless of how widespread these evening showers wind up being. The lack of a wind shift will keep temperatures and humidity above normal into Friday. However, conditions look mainly dry with our region sitting between an inverted trough to our east and an incoming upper level low to our west. Most likely rainfall amounts being offered are mainly 0.1" to 0.33", but with convective nature of some of the rain, footprints will be quite variable. KEY MESSAGE 3: Upper level troughing will likely settle over eastern Canada and the Northeast as the longwave pattern is favored to stall Saturday through the weekend. Model consensus points to multiple rounds of rainfall associated with upper level low overhead and potential for surface low pressure to gyre and pivot back westward early next week while a series of troughs move through the base of the longwave overhead. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Wednesday! Wednesday could start with a bit of leftover cloud cover, but we get more sunshine going through the day. With that sun, it’ll feel a lot more like September than early November as sunshine sends our temperatures soaring into the low and mid-70s. This will be warm enough to break or tie records all across the area. Clouds start to fill back in by Wednesday night, as lows fall back into the 50s. Thursday morning looks to start dry for most, before showers begin to roll through from west to east in the mid to late morning hours. Right now, it looks like we all see rain, but it’s not a ton with most only running a couple tenths of an inch of new rain. Temperatures are a tad cooler with most in the low to mid-60s. Friday looks drier, but there could still be a spotty shower here and there. We continue to lose a little bit of ground temperature wise, as most talk high temperatures in the upper 50s and lower 60s. The weekend could again feature a few showers for Saturday. Temperatures turn noticeably cooler with most only in the 40s to about 50 for Saturday afternoon. Sunday looks drier, but again could feature a spotty morning shower or two. Temperatures are generally stuck in the 40s for most.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-03T22:30:00Z — same caveat): Sun and record warmth for some Wednesday — Wednesday turns much warmer, as highs reach the low to mid-70s region-wide. A couple towns may approach 80! Some towns likely set a new daily record high. Expect a partly to mostly sunny sky, with a noticeable south breeze. Thursday stays mild, with highs in the mid-60s. An approaching cold front brings a mostly cloudy sky and scattered showers. A late evening thunderstorm cannot be ruled out in southern Vermont. The south breeze becomes a bit stronger, with gusts near 30. Friday turns drier, with only a spot shower leftover. A few hours of sunshine are likely, before clouds thicken up through the afternoon. Highs again reach the 60s. This weekend turns much cooler, an an upper-level low sends highs back closer to 50. Expect lots of clouds with a few additional showers, especially on Saturday.
